findings.description: Verify payload caps remain fail-open. The capped ledger is re-carried only from a schema-usable prior object, while payload truncation merely sets findings verdict/RVERDICT to CHANGES_NEEDED. Custom CLAUDE.md migration remains lossy. The capped-ledger re-carry fixes valid prior ledgers but still fails open for schema-corrupt, parseable state. Validate the prior file with the full findings schema before prompt construction or merging.

The new guard does not add an open blocking finding or a separate non-promotable state; after rewriting the raw verdict to CHANGES_NEEDED, line 2105 deterministically converts it to APPROVED when the reviewer returned no project blocker. [DUAL-PASS blocker] FAIL-OPEN (new in this diff): the verify-round open-findings ledger is now capped (`vmaxf`, default 40, env-overridable via PLINTH_VERIFY_MAX_FINDINGS) and nothing re-injects the dropped items. The reviewer's findings-$r.json is the ONLY input to the verdict arithmetic (`blocking="$(jq ... findings-$r.json)"` at ~line 2011) — findings that were never shown to the model cannot appear in its output, so they are silently DROPPED from the open set instead of staying open. Scenario: round 1 reports 45 open blocking findings; round 2 sends the top 40 by rank, the model resolves all 40, findings-2.json contains 40 resolved items, blocking=0 → APPROVED + mint_receipt for a SHA with 5 never-re-checked blockers. The prompt text 'Other open findings remain open — do not invent resolutions' is not enforceable: the model cannot emit items it never saw. Same class, same function: (a) `prior="$(jq ... || echo '[]')"` — a missing/corrupt findings-$((r-1)).json degrades to an EMPTY ledger and every prior open finding vanishes with no error; (b) PLINTH_VERIFY_MAX_FINDINGS=1 in the driver's environment collapses the ledger to one item, so a trusted-but-fallible driver can accidentally (or a stale export can silently) erase its own blockers. Fix: after each verify round, merge any open prior finding that the round did not adjudicate back into findings-$r.json as status=open (and fail closed when the ledger jq errors) rather than relying on the model to carry them. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

[DUAL-PASS blocker] FAIL-OPEN (new in this diff): the verify payload is hard-truncated mid-diff (`vpayload="${vpayload:0:$vmaxb}"`, default 400000 bytes) and the round can still produce a BINDING APPROVED. Nothing records the truncation in verdict.json — only a NOTE inside the prompt — so mint_receipt stamps APPROVED@sha with a diff_digest computed over the FULL diff while an arbitrary tail of the branch was never shown to any reviewer. Scenario: a 900KB cumulative fix diff; the last 500KB (which contains a new fail-open in the ship gate) is cut; the reviewer sees only the head, marks the prior findings resolved, verdict APPROVED, receipt minted, PR ships. This directly contradicts the coverage story the same block claims ('full read at the anchor plus this diff = the whole branch'). At minimum: record `truncated:true,truncated_bytes:N` in verdict.json and refuse to bind APPROVED on a truncated payload (fall back to a fresh full round or split the diff), instead of degrading silently. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

[DUAL-PASS blocker] REAL BUG that stops the loop — the new `git status --porcelain -z` record parser mis-parses every SINGLE-SIDED status, defeating the NEEDS-HUMAN.md / HANDOFF.md exemptions. The pattern `[MADRCUT?!][MADRCUT?!]\ *` requires BOTH status columns to be a letter, but porcelain XY uses SPACE for the unchanged side: an unstaged modification is ' M path' and a staged-only one is 'M  path'. Neither matches, so the code falls to `*) path="$entry"` and path becomes ' M NEEDS-HUMAN.md' — which matches none of the exempt cases → dirty=1 → `die "working tree is dirty"`. Consequences: (1) the driver is REQUIRED to maintain NEEDS-HUMAN.md, so the normal state (tracked file, modified, unstaged) now makes review.sh refuse to run at all; (2) review.sh itself writes HANDOFF.md at the end of every run (new `plinth handoff` calls at ~2140/2280), so a tracked HANDOFF.md guarantees ' M HANDOFF.md' on the next run and the newly-added HANDOFF exemption never fires. The old `path="${entry:3}"` handled all of these. Only both-sided codes ('??', 'MM', 'AM') parse correctly today. Note: this code is identical in the installed twin `.plinth/review.sh:116` (both blobs are ce3aa4c) — this PR is what installs it as THIS repo's instrument, so the breakage lands here on the next review. Fix: strip the first 3 bytes when the record is a status record and track rename records positionally (a rename emits `XY new\0orig\0`), rather than pattern-matching the status letters. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

[DUAL-PASS major] FAIL-OPEN, SIGPIPE-under-pipefail class — the same class this diff fixes for `jq|head` in _reviewer_codex, reintroduced in two new floors. (1) `if [ "$RISK" = "0" ] && printf '%s\n' "$_tool_names" | grep -Eq "$HARNESS_RE"` (~612): `grep -q` exits at the FIRST match; git's dot-prefixed paths (.github/, .plinth/) sort first, so the match is early. If `$_tool_names` exceeds the 64KB pipe buffer (a branch touching >~1500 files), the writer blocks, grep closes the pipe, the writer dies with SIGPIPE, pipefail makes the pipeline status 141, the condition reads FALSE and the SELF-REFERENTIAL TOOLING FLOOR is skipped — the exact Tier-0 bypass the comment says it prevents. (2) `if git diff --name-only "${base_tip}...HEAD" 2>/dev/null | grep -qx 'VERSION'` (~856): same mechanism silently skips the new VERSION↔CHANGELOG floor, leaving a mismatched release at Tier 0. Checked the other new `| grep -q` sites: the `grep -qxF '.plinth/risk-classify.sh'` elif (~589) fails toward the SAFE branch (base-blob classifier) and `git log -1 | grep -qiE` (~1707) has bounded output, so only these two fail open. Fix: test against the already-materialized variable without a pipe (`case`/`[[ =~ ]]`), or drain the writer as `cfg()` now does. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

[DUAL-PASS major] DATA LOSS in the new `plinth update` CLAUDE.md migration, two distinct paths. (1) `_driver_project_is_scaffold` (~228) shells out to python3 with `|| true` and treats an EMPTY body as 'scaffold'. If python3 is absent, errors, or the heredoc fails for any reason, body='' → returns 0 (scaffold) → `_migrate_custom_claude_into_driver_project` takes the `mv "$extracted" "$dest"` branch and OVERWRITES an existing, non-scaffold `.plinth/DRIVER-project.md`, destroying every operator note in it — the exact file the NOTE it replaced told users to move their rules into. A missing interpreter must not read as 'this file is empty'; check `command -v python3` and fail closed to the append branch. (2) The extraction awk drops all content BEFORE the first `^# ` line: a CLAUDE.md that opens with 'IMPORTANT: never drop the prod DB' and only later has an H1 loses that first line entirely, and because the 5-line banner plus any single extracted line already exceeds the `-lt 6` guard, the full-file fallback does not fire — then CLAUDE.md is overwritten by the pinned shell, so the rule is gone from both files. The canary (#21) and the workflow cases only exercise files derived from the stock old template, so neither path is covered. Also: the comment claims the awk drops the stock 'You are the implementer…' preamble; trace the rules on the very fixture in the test (H1 → blank → preamble → '## Project-specific notes') and rule 4 `seen_h1 && !keep && NF` sets keep=1 on the preamble line, so it IS copied — a comment claim the code does not back. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

[DUAL-PASS major] REAL BUG — plan --deep decides a seat is 'unavailable' by CONTENT-SNIFFING the review body, so a legitimate review that discusses authentication is discarded along with all its blockers. Two sites implement the same rule: `_plan_seat_output_ok` (~5214) returns failure when the seat's stdout matches 'not logged in|please run /login|seat .+ unavailable', and the merge python's `unavail_re` (~5397) marks the seat `available:false` on the same patterns plus 'binary not found'. The seat most likely to emit those words is the security_ops seat: a blocker such as 'the plan never says what the API returns when the caller is not logged in' makes its own seat read as an auth failure. Effect chain: `_plan_seat_output_ok` fails → a full sequential retry is burned → still 'fails' → the seat's blockers/questions/nits are skipped entirely by the `if not s.get('available'): continue` harvest loop → status drops to incomplete/empty → the NEEDS-HUMAN [BLOCKING] append is skipped for status=empty → a genuine security blocker is silently dropped and the handoff tells the human to go fix their CLI login. Classify availability from the process rc and the classifier's bounded stderr (which `_plan_seat_classify` already computes), not from the model's prose. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

The same masking hides the new same-open soft cap, which exits via die_infra after findings exist. Surface a distinct state (e.g. verdict:null + reviewer_verdict + incomplete:true) and never clear last_error on the strength of a findings file. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

[DUAL-PASS major] The deterministic thrash policy overrides the ratified PRECEDENCE rule and can demote BLOCKERS. `is_out_of_scope_demote` is `is_outside_delta and (is_external_security|not) and (is_thrash_class or ($phase=="build" and ($mode=="verify" or "resume")))` — so in any BUILD verify/resume round, ANY new finding on a file outside the fix delta that is not caught by the `is_external_security` keyword/path regex is rewritten to severity minor, and the enclosing map admits `.severity == "blocker"` (`elif (.severity != "major" and .severity != "blocker") then .`). Both contracts state the opposite and state it as overriding: 'a finding in a BUILD-phase blocking class — spec violation, real bug, data loss, fail-open in a claimed guarantee, enforcement overclaim, missing test for changed behavior — BLOCKS whenever it is discovered, in any round, on any line.' Scenario: round 2 discovers a data-corrupting bug in shared/dashboard/smoke-snapshot.sh (not a security-surface path, description has no 'data loss'/'injection'/'auth' keyword) on a file the fix commit did not touch → demoted to minor → blocking=0 → APPROVED. `is_external_security` is a keyword filter over reviewer prose, which is not a sound proxy for 'is this a blocking class'. Related weakening in the same file: `sticky_process_findings` auto-flips reviewer-reported OPEN majors to RESOLVED ('[AUTO-STICKY: …]') whenever a thrash-class fingerprint matches a ledger entry and the file blob is unchanged — a real 'coverage remains incomplete: the new empty-merge branch has no test' finding matches class:coverage-gap while missing `is_real_test_gap_desc`, so a genuine missing-test-for-changed-behavior finding is auto-resolved. (Pre-existing in shared/ at base; this diff is what installs it as this repo's instrument, which is why I am raising it here.) [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]

[DUAL-PASS major] ERROR-CATCHING GAP + claim growth in the new delegation before-sha. The code validates only the SHAPE of `$dbefore` (`^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,64}$`) and then prints it back verbatim; it never checks that the object exists, that it is a commit, or that it equals the repo's HEAD at receipt time. A lane does not commit, so `git rev-parse HEAD` at delegation time IS the pre-run HEAD — the verification is one command away and is simply not done. The failure this is supposed to catch is precisely a fallible-lane mistake (pasting a stale OUT path from a prior invocation together with that run's stale sha, or a truncated/garbled sha); today both record a green `before=` receipt indistinguishable from a bound one. Meanwhile the shipped implementer docs escalate the claim: shared/.claude/agents/grok-implementer.md:193 and shared/.claude/agents/codex-implementer.md:169 now say 'Pass the literal BEFORE sha from step 0 as the 4th argument so the receipt is bound to THIS run (not a stale OUT paste)' and 'STATUS: complete without a receipt line that includes before=<BEFORE> is a false report' — which reads as a verified binding, while lane-guard's own header (correctly) says only 'at least labeled with the wrong run's HEAD'. Overclaiming is this repo's flagged recurrent defect class. Either verify (`git cat-file -e "$dbefore^{commit}"` and compare to HEAD, exit 3 on mismatch) or bring the two agent docs down to the header's honest wording. [VERIFY-CARRY: not in capped ledger / not re-adjudicated — remains open]
